page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.s2.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor and the x86_64 CPU architecture. It features 2 dedicated virtual processor cores and 8.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB of memory per core. The instance operates without bundled hardware accelerators, maintaining a zero GPU configuration.

The instance does not include integrated local disk storage, necessitating the attachment of external block storage for operating system persistence and application data. It also includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, which requires networking provisions such as Elastic IP or NAT gateways for external network access. From a resource-allocation perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation provides predictable processing capacity without the variability found in burstable or shared-core tiers, offering consistent resource efficiency for baseline operational demands.

Given its balanced dual-core configuration and 8.0 GB RAM footprint, Alibaba Cloud ecs.s2.xlarge fits low-to-moderate computational tasks. Best-fit use cases include small web servers, microservices, continuous integration runners, lightweight application backends, and low-traffic transactional databases operating alongside attached cloud storage.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.s2.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 processor architecture and the KVM hypervisor. The instance is configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs and 8.0 GB of RAM, yielding an even 1:4 CPU-to-memory allocation of 4.0 GB per core. The system contains no physical GPUs and does not come with integrated local storage, requiring network-attached storage for system volumes and runtime data storage. Additionally, zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default. Because the vCPUs are dedicated, processing capability remains steady without CPU credit or throttling constraints. With its balanced resource profile, ecs.s2.xlarge is designed for lightweight and medium-density enterprise tasks, such as running application servers, staging environments, API gateways, internal development environments, and low-scale relational databases.
